title: Ember and Veil Anew
premise: Gideon Amberdale, a temple scribe hiding her magic behind sold charms and forged ledgers, is unmasked when the usurper King Vessic's witch-hunters raid the Scriptorium of Ashen Vale. Fleeing with a stolen covenant-stone, she joins a smuggler crew bound for the free cities, where she learns she is the last living signatory's heir—the only person who can reforge the broken Ember-Veil covenant that once kept both realms alive. Betrayed by her closest ally, hunted by a hunter who was once her friend, Gideon must choose between sealing the Veil forever (saving her world but dooming the ember-realm) or sacrificing her own name and memory to bind both. She chooses sacrifice: the covenant reforged through her erasure, though a single ember-charm bearing her handwriting survives to hint she existed.
about_author: Ivo Oyelaran is a former archivist from Lagos who writes fantasy about bureaucracies, faith, and the people history forgets to record. 'Ember and Veil Anew' is the second novel in the Ember and Veil sequence.

chapters.title: Ink That Should Not Glow
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. In the occupied city of Ashen Vale, Gideon sells illegal charms disguised as blessings, hiding her gift beneath scribe's routine work. When a customer's charm flares visible light in a market square, she realizes someone reported her. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath practiced calm.

chapters.title: The Proclamation
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The usurper Vessic's criers announce a realm-wide hunt for the gifted, offering silver for denunciations. Gideon burns her charm-stock but keeps one stone she cannot explain—her dead mother's covenant-token. Beat: fear sharpening into stubbornness.

chapters.title: Raid on the Scriptorium
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Witch-hunters, led by Captain Serah Vole (Gideon's childhood friend), storm the Scriptorium. Gideon escapes through the archive stacks as her mentor Brannoc is taken. Beat: guilt and grief; the past literally burning behind her.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Price
chapters.summary: Tamsin Roe's POV. River-smuggler Tamsin agrees to carry a fugitive scribe downstream for an outrageous fee, sensing Gideon's stone is worth more than coin. Beat: wary transactional trust with an undercurrent of curiosity.

chapters.title: What the Stone Remembers
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. On the river, the covenant-stone activates near an old Veil-shrine, showing Gideon visions of the original signing—and her mother among the signatories. Beat: awe curdling into the weight of inheritance.

chapters.title: Hounds of the Hunt
chapters.summary: Serah Vole's POV. Serah tracks Gideon, torn between duty to Vessic's regime that feeds her soldiers' families and memory of the girl who once shared her books. Beat: loyalty bending under truth.

chapters.title: The Free City of Duskharbor
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Arriving in Duskharbor, Gideon seeks the Covenant Council, only to find it fractured—some want the Veil sealed, some want it broken for power. Beat: disillusionment; sanctuary is not safety.

chapters.title: Lessons in Broken Magic
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Exiled mage Ondrell teaches Gideon how covenants are reforged: a signatory must give something irreplaceable. Gideon practices small bindings and fails painfully. Beat: humility and determination.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Court
chapters.summary: King Vessic's POV. Vessic reveals he wants the Veil broken deliberately—the ember-realm's dying fire can fuel his armies if channeled. He promotes Serah to hunt-captain general. Beat: chilling ambition; the antagonist's logic made sympathetic-adjacent.

chapters.title: An Old Debt Called In
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin's old creditor betrays the crew's route to Vessic's hunters to clear his own family's names. Tamsin must choose between fleeing and warning Gideon. Beat: loyalty tested by survival.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Saltmarsh Shrine
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Hunters ambush the crew at a shrine needed for the reforging ritual. Gideon uses her gift openly for the first time, saving Tamsin but confirming her identity to Serah across the battlefield. Beat: exhilaration followed by exposure.

chapters.title: Serah's Summons
chapters.summary: Serah's POV. Serah corners Gideon alone and offers escape: surrender quietly, testify against the Council, live. Gideon refuses, revealing what Vessic truly plans for the ember-realm. Beat: heartbreak; friendship ends so truth can begin.

chapters.title: The Council of Ashes
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Gideon presents proof of Vessic's plan to the Council; half walk out, calling it fabrication. Ondrell confesses he helped break the original covenant years ago. Beat: betrayal upon betrayal; resolve hardens anyway.

chapters.title: Into the Veil
chapters.summary: Gideon and Tamsin's alternating POV. The pair cross into the ember-realm through a thin place, finding a dying world of cooling hearths and fading spirits who remember Gideon's mother. Beat: wonder and sorrow entwined.

chapters.title: The Last Signatory
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. An ember-spirit elder reveals the full cost: reforging requires a signatory's name, memory, and self, erased from both realms. Gideon hides this from Tamsin. Beat: secret burden; the price of survival becomes literal.

chapters.title: Vessic Marches
chapters.summary: Multiple brief POVs (Serah, Tamsin, a soldier). Vessic's army moves on Duskharbor; Serah, having verified Gideon's claims in captured documents, wavers at her orders. Beat: rising dread; the hunter turning.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Ledger
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Ondrell sells the ritual site's location to Vessic, believing a broken Veil under controlled terms saves more lives. Gideon confronts him; he dies defending her from hunters, whispering an apology. Beat: bitter forgiveness too late.

chapters.title: Battle for the Thin Place
chapters.summary: Gideon, Tamsin, and Serah's POVs converge. Duskharbor's defenders hold the shrine approach while Gideon begins the rite; Serah openly defects, shielding Gideon from Vessic's elite. Beat: chaos, sacrifice, alliances remade in fire.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. At the covenant-stone, Gideon speaks the old words and offers her name. Vessic interrupts, trying to seize the binding; the covenant accepts Gideon's sacrifice instead, and the Veil blazes closed around his stolen power. Beat: transcendent climax; identity dissolving.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Name
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The battle won, Tamsin searches for Gideon and finds no one remembers her—not even the stones. Only a half-burned charm in Tamsin's pocket bears familiar handwriting. Beat: devastating tenderness.

chapters.title: Ember and Veil Anew
chapters.summary: Ensemble epilogue POV. The free cities rebuild; Serah leads a new order guarding the shrines; the ember-realm slowly warms. Tamsin keeps the charm and tells its story to anyone who'll listen. Beat: bittersweet renewal.

chapters.title: A Handwriting on the Wind
chapters.summary: Final chapter, unnamed POV. Somewhere beyond the Veil, a presence without a name feels drawn to a river, a city, a smuggler's voice telling stories—and a faint warmth answers when it listens. Beat: ambiguous, hopeful grace note suggesting identity may be reforged too.
